what: Figures cited from outside this lab, recorded as a receipt so that papers citing them are grounded in something a reader can check.
provenance_warning: SECOND-HAND. Every number here was transcribed or recomputed from a published external artifact on 2026-09-01. None of it was measured by this lab. Fields tagged as_printed are quoted from the paper; fields tagged recomputed_by_us were derived by re-running arithmetic over the authors' own published CSV files. A transcription is not a measurement and this receipt does not make it one.

pr_mci_study.identity: Gong, Pinna, Bian, Zhang. 'Analyzing Message-Code Inconsistency in AI Coding Agent-Authored Pull Requests'. MSR 2026 Mining Challenge Track.
pr_mci_study.replication_repo_license: NONE FOUND. The GitHub API reports license: null and there is no LICENSE file in the tree. The paper is CC BY 4.0 and AIDev is CC-BY-4.0, but the replication repo itself carries no explicit grant. Cite it; do not redistribute it.

corpus.derivation: AIDev-pop subset (33,596 PRs across 2,807 repos with >100 stars), filtered to closed PRs under a permissive licence.

high_mci.WHAT_IT_IS_NOT: This is the FIRING RATE OF A HEURISTIC, not a human-validated prevalence of inconsistency. high-MCI is a threshold on a hand-built score s = 0.3*s_scope + 0.4*s_filetype + 0.3*s_tasktype, none of whose terms reads a diff against a description. Writing '1.7% of agentic PRs are inconsistent' misquotes this study.
high_mci.defensible_phrasing: 1.7% of 23,247 agentic PRs were flagged high-MCI by a heuristic, of which 246 (60.6%) were confirmed misaligned by the authors' own annotators.

annotations.location: results/all_annotations_with_taxonomy.csv (2.14 MB), plus 974 per-PR markdown packets under data/manual_annotations/
annotations.why_this_matters_to_us: A public human-labelled set means precision against third-party labels can be measured WITHOUT this lab convening its own blind panel. That is a stronger design than the one we have been using, because the labeller has no stake in our instrument.

phantom_changes.DENOMINATOR_CORRECTION: 45.4% is of the 432 manually classified partial/misaligned PRs — NOT of 23,247 and NOT of 406. The authors' own README carries the check line 'Verify: Phantom Changes should be 45.4% (196/432)'. Rescaled against the whole corpus it is 196/23,247 = 0.84%.
phantom_changes.operational_definition: The annotators' checkbox reads verbatim: 'Phantom Changes: Description claims changes were made, but no files were actually modified (zero files changed)'. It is an EMPTY-DIFF test, not a semantic mismatch test.
phantom_changes.enrichment_caveat: Splitting the 432 by batch, the 134 drawn from the 600-PR validation sample are only 9.7% phantom_changes (13/134), where the top category is understated_scope at 38.8%. The headline 45.4% is therefore substantially an artifact of the detector's enrichment for zero-diff PRs.

their_detector.positive_class: misaligned only (42 of 600); 'partial' collapsed into aligned
their_detector.THRESHOLD_DISCREPANCY: The paper states the operating threshold is 0.61 while printing P 0.742 / R 0.548 / F1 0.630, which their own validation/validation_metrics.json labels as the 0.60 operating point. Reported as observed; we have not asked the authors and do not assert which is intended.

precision_over_the_complete_flagged_set.note: NOT a number the paper reports. Recomputed by us by joining their published flags to their published labels. It is measurable at all only because all 406 flags were annotated.

the_two_arms.note: The single most decision-relevant finding for this lab. Their accusation is really two instruments with very different precision, separated by whether the PR contains a diff at all.

arm_a_zero_diff.reading: accusing a PR that changed no files is close to trivially correct

the_two_arms.arm_b_reading: Accusing a PR that ACTUALLY CONTAINS A DIFF scores 0.136 strict against the authors' own annotations.
the_two_arms.COMPARISON_DISCIPLINE: Our V14 path-claim accusation scored 0.16 against our own blind panel. These two numbers are close, and the convergence is suggestive rather than probative: different corpora slices, different claim units, different labelling instruments, different positive-class rules. Do NOT report them as a replication. What they jointly support is only that the non-trivial case is hard for both.

aidev_corpus.cited_as: Li, Zhang, Hassan, 'The Rise of AI Teammates in Software Engineering (SE) 3.0', arXiv 2507.15003
aidev_corpus.card_version_note: The card currently describes v4 (2,743,854 PRs, 327,477 repositories). The PR-MCI paper never names the AIDev version, tag or snapshot date it used; that is recorded below as unverified.

unverified: Which AIDev version the PR-MCI paper used. The full text names no version, tag or snapshot date.
Provenance of 127 templated failure_evidence strings in the 432-row taxonomy CSV, all of the form 'Assigned as <category> based on mismatch between description and patch details.'
Whether a corpus-wide human base rate can be reconstructed from their sampling design; it used two-stage sampling and the weights needed to unbias it were not located.
Whether the replication repo's annotations are licensed for reuse; no LICENSE file exists.

Whether the two annotators were blind to the detector score. Sampling-script comments say scores were used for stratification only and three packets read contained no score, but only 3 of 974 packets were inspected.
Any Claude Code agent-specific rate. The paper's own threats-to-validity notes ~220 Claude Code PRs and 2 high-MCI PRs; no agent-level figure from this study is meaningful for that agent.
